plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant five-petaled blossoms on bare branches before the leaves emerge. It is widely cultivated in East Asian gardens and is prized for its early-season beauty and sweet scent.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (late January to March)
plants.location: Japan, China, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms herald the end of winter in East Asia and are celebrated before cherry blossoms; the fruit is pickled into umeboshi and used to make umeshu liqueur.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler yellow petals. It carpets woodlands and meadows in early spring and is the ancestor of many garden daffodils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to April)
plants.location: Western Europe, including England, Wales, France and Spain; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant contain toxic alkaloids, including galantamine, which has been developed into a medication for Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: An evergreen tree or large shrub covered in fluffy, fragrant golden flower balls. It is a hardy pioneer species of southeastern Australian woodlands and is Australia's national floral emblem.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in Australia (July to October), with some related Acacia species flowering in late summer and autumn
plants.funFact: Wattle Day is celebrated in Australia on September 1, and the green and gold of the sporting teams are derived from the wattle.

plants.name: Rhododendron arboreum
plants.description: A large evergreen shrub or small tree that bears dense, rounded clusters of bell-shaped flowers. It grows in Himalayan mountain forests and begins blooming as spring arrives at middle elevations.
plants.location: Himalayas of Nepal, India, Bhutan and Sri Lanka
plants.funFact: It is the national flower of Nepal, where the petals are eaten in salads and used to make a tangy juice and traditional medicines.
